Wikipedia independently corroborates the larger figure: 'Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Company, LP is an approximately 6,300-mile natural gas interstate pipeline system.' So there are two internally-consistent CURRENT candidates -- ~1,300 mi (route/corridor) or ~6,000-6,300 mi (total installed pipe, the figure PEPL itself reports as 'Miles of Pipelines' and that Wikipedia echoes) -- and NEITHER is 860. Either way, 860 is wrong for a currently-operating characterization of the line and should not stand uncorrected. Proposed refs (both verified, both name Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line specifically): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/76063/000007606322000010/pepl-20211231.htm and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panhandle_Eastern.

REX's stated length has genuinely changed over time as laterals/receipt points were added (this is a real length-genealogy issue, not just noisy reporting): ~1,323 mi at the original 2005-2006 open-season stage (naturalgasintel.com, 2006-03-01, describing only the then-firm-committed mainline); 1,663 mi at the 2005 FERC-filing stage (naturalgasintel search results); 1,679 mi widely cited for the completed 2009 system (Wikipedia infobox; the row's own cited hydrocarbons-technology/offshore-technology page after its 2026 redirect; SEC KMP 424B5 2008 prospectus supplement, sec.gov, verified, describes REX as 'extending from Opal, Wyoming and Meeker, Colorado to Clarington, Ohio' at that stage); 1,712 mi in a Tallgrass SEC 8-K exhibit filed 2017-01-17 (sec.gov, verified); and 1,714 mi in the CURRENT (2024) disclosure -- Phillips 66's own divestiture announcement describes REX as a '1,714-mile pipeline system,' independently confirmed word-for-word by both Oil & Gas Journal and Rigzone (both verified, both name the pipeline). None of these five figures is 1685. The 1,714 figure is both the most recent and the most authoritative (stated by the pipeline's own owner in its own 2024 SEC-adjacent disclosure), so it is the best current value, but flagging as a concern rather than a clean fill because GEM's own convention for which vintage of a growing system to record is not something I can adjudicate alone -- Baird should confirm whether 1685 was ever a real intermediate figure or is simply a transcription of one of the other numbers.

resolutions.recommendation: re-verify Capacity; 4050 MMcf/d does not match any capacity figure found in current sourcing, and the pipeline's true 'capacity' is not a single number (it differs by direction and has grown through several enhancement projects)
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=4050 MMcf/d. I could not find ANY source stating 4050/4,050 MMcf/d for REX, and REX's capacity is not well represented by one number: original west-to-east design capacity was 1.8 Bcf/d (SEC 424B5 2008, verified; Rigzone 2024 article, verified, states the same 'design capacity' figure); the Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project raised EAST-TO-WEST capacity in Zone 3 specifically to 2.6 Bcf/d (SEC 8-K exhibit 2017, verified; EIA todayinenergy article, verified, describes the buildout toward that figure in increments); and as of the 2024 ownership sale, Phillips 66/OGJ/Rigzone (all verified) describe REX as providing 'over 5 Bcf/d of bi-directional' service -- i.e. the two directions summed, not a single nameplate figure. 1.8+2.6=4.4 Bcf/d, still not 4.05, and 'over 5 Bcf/d bidirectional' is a different kind of figure (combined throughput capability, not unidirectional design capacity) from what GEM's single Capacity field implies. Left the candidate value blank rather than guess which of these numbers GEM intends; recommend Baird decide whether Capacity should record the original 1.8 Bcf/d west-to-east design capacity (1800 MMcf/d), the current >5000 MMcf/d bidirectional figure, or something else, then re-source accordingly.

resolutions.recommendation: no existence/classification/status action needed; note chronic low utilization in ResearcherNotes
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguous. Confirmed via the original FERC certificate docket CP09-54 (Federal Register Notice of Application, filed Jan 27, 2009 by Ruby Pipeline, L.L.C.), EIA's Historical Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (row 'Ruby Pipeline Project', Docket CP09-54, Regulatory Agency FERC, Status 'Completed', in-service 2011-07-28), Wikipedia, and a current (issued/effective June 10, 2026) FERC Gas Tariff filed by 'Ruby Pipeline, L.L.C.' that repeatedly references 'the Docket No. CP09-54-000 facilities' -- proving this is a live, actively-tariffed FERC asset today, not a phantom/GEM-only entry. CLASSIFICATION: correctly transmission/interstate gas, not gathering -- 683-mile, 42-inch interstate mainline with FERC-jurisdictional tariff, multiple receipt/delivery interconnects (Opal Hub area and Malin-area interconnects per the tariff's point tables). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster -- no other row shares this Opal(WY)-to-Malin(OR) route; not a duplicate of Cheyenne Plains/Cheyenne Connector/Kern River/Mojave/GTN or any other West-batch pipeline. STATUS: 'operating' is correct and current, but the batch brief's own flag (post-bankruptcy reduced service) is real and worth recording: Ruby has been chronically underutilized since shortly after start-up (NGI, 2011: initial flows only 4.3% of the 1.5 Bcf/d design capacity) and remains so today -- Wikipedia states roughly 50% utilization 'as of 2026', while an independent midstream-analyst source (East Daley Analytics) states 2025 throughput averaged only 208 MMcf/d, i.e. ~14% of capacity, attributing the weakness to competing Canadian gas imports into the Pacific Northwest. Both sources agree the line is NOT idled or converted -- it continues interstate FIRM/interruptible transportation service under its live FERC tariff -- so this is a utilization caveat, not a status change. Citation-pool coverage: of the 16 harvested wiki citations, I opened/resolved bit.ly/2kFqoiK (-> en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Pipeline), prnewswire.com (bankruptcy filing), and attempted reuters.com (401 bot-wall, unresolved -- archive.org's CDX API was itself rate-limited (429) for the whole session so no Wayback fallback could be tried) and businesswire.com x2 + blankrome.com (403/429 bot-walls; blankrome's response body was a Vercel bot-checkpoint page, not the article, on every retry). eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is a generic landing page (not pipeline-specific) so I used the more specific eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=3210 article and the EIA pipeline-projects workbook instead. kindermorgan.com's 2018-vintage Ruby page and blm.gov's project page were not opened -- deprioritized once independent corroboration for every data point was already in hand from other sources; neither is needed to support or contradict any value here.

resolutions.recommendation: update Owner1 to 'Tallgrass Energy' (Owner1% stays 100.00%) -- Ruby Pipeline LLC is the asset-holding SPV, not a corporate owner, and its parent has changed twice since the current entry was last touched
resolutions.researcher_notes: Owner1 = 'Ruby Pipeline LLC [100%]' is the SAME defect pattern the batch brief flags for P0151 Alliance: an operating/holding-entity name sitting in the Owner slot rather than the corporate owner. 'Ruby Pipeline, L.L.C.' is genuinely real -- it is the FERC certificate-holder and tariff-filer (see the Operator fill below) -- but it has never been an independent company; it has always been wholly owned by a rotating cast of corporate parents: El Paso Corporation (2009 FERC application, 100%) -> a 50/50 JV structure after El Paso brought in a partner during construction (SEC 8-K, El Paso Pipeline Partners, 2010) -> Kinder Morgan inherited El Paso's share when KM acquired El Paso Corp in 2012 -> Veresen Inc. acquired the other (non-KM) 50% for $1.425bn in 2014 (Hart Energy, 'Veresen Acquires 50% Of Northwest Ruby Pipeline'), later folded into Pembina when Pembina acquired Veresen (2017) -> Ruby Pipeline LLC (both KM's and Pembina's 50% stakes) filed Chapter 11 on March 31, 2022 (PR Newswire: 'a natural gas pipeline joint venture between Kinder Morgan, Inc. and Pembina Pipeline Corporation'; KMI continued operating it through the case) -> Tallgrass MLP Operations, LLC won Ruby at the bankruptcy auction for $282.5 million (East Daley Analytics) and completed the 100% acquisition on/about January 13, 2023 (Pipeline & Gas Journal: 'Tallgrass Completes Ruby Pipeline Acquisition, Adds 682 Miles of Infrastructure to Portfolio' -- 'Tallgrass is now the 100% owner following the completion of this acquisition from Kinder Morgan and Pembina'; Tallgrass's own newsroom release confirms the same close; Wikipedia independently corroborates the $282M bankruptcy sale to 'Tallgrass Energy Partners, a Blackstone Group company'). Three independent origins (Pipeline & Gas Journal trade press, East Daley Analytics -- an independent midstream research firm, and Wikipedia) all agree the CURRENT (since Jan 2023) 100% owner is Tallgrass -- this is now nearly 3.5 years stale on the sheet. Matches the exact naming convention already staged on sibling row P0208 (Tallgrass Interstate Gas Transmission) in this same batch: Owner1='Tallgrass Energy' is the ultimate-parent brand name, distinct from the FERC-certificated operating subsidiary (which stays 'Ruby Pipeline, L.L.C.' in Operator).

resolutions.recommendation: update SegmentCost -- GEM's $2.96bn is the ORIGINAL (2009) pre-construction estimate; multiple independent sources put the actual/final project cost at roughly $3.5-3.65bn after well-documented 2010-2011 delays and overruns
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's current SegmentCost (2,960,000,000 USD) exactly matches EIA's Historical Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Cost=2960, same Docket CP09-54 row) -- but that is precisely the problem: both appear to carry forward Ruby's ORIGINAL 2009 FERC-filing-era cost estimate, not the as-built figure. Contemporaneous 2011 reporting documents a specific, sourced cost increase: El Paso Corp. raised its Ruby cost estimate 18% (a $590 million increase) to $3.55 billion in February 2011, citing permitting delays, additional cultural-resource survey/mitigation work, and litigation (Bloomberg, 'El Paso Boosts Ruby Pipeline Cost Estimates, Delays Start,' 2011-02-24 -- could not verify this specific URL directly, blocked 403, but the same $3.55bn figure for the SAME Feb-2011 revised estimate is independently stated by Natural Gas Intelligence's contemporaneous reporting, which I did verify and read directly: 'The $3.55 billion Ruby Pipeline, which has a capacity of 1.5 Bcf/d...'). Oregon Public Broadcasting's 2011 in-service story independently corroborates a cost in the same range: 'Ruby Pipeline To Open After $3.5 Billion And One Year's Work.' A third, independent project-database source (Offshore Technology / formerly Hydrocarbons Technology, a market-intelligence publisher unconnected to El Paso/Kinder Morgan/Tallgrass) states the somewhat higher final figure '$3.65bn' as the total project cost. All three of these independent origins (NGI's 2011 news reporting, OPB's 2011 news reporting, and the Offshore Technology project database) agree the true cost is materially above GEM's $2.96bn -- by 18-23%, well past the >=10%-of-value threshold for a material spec conflict. I'm proposing $3,650,000,000 (the more specific, latest-stated total-investment figure) as the candidate, while flagging in this note that the two 2011-vintage independent sources instead support $3,550,000,000 -- a researcher should pick whichever figure best matches GEM's SegmentCostYear convention (proposal-estimate vs. final-cost) once that column is set. Either way, $2.96bn is stale.

CONTESTED (Status / EndState/Province / Location): GEM records Status=operating with EndState/Province=California and EndLocation implying the pipeline still reaches California. It does not. The historic ~700-mile Southern Trails system (converted ARCO Four Corners Line 90, crude-to-gas, Docket CP99-163-000) had two California-touching pieces: a never-activated West Zone (Essex, CA to Long Beach, CA, ~209 mi, certificate later vacated/abandoned by FERC, c. 2004-05) and a California sliver of the East Zone. FERC authorized abandonment-in-place of the East Zone's California-to-Arizona segments (~220 mi) in Docket CP17-__ / the 2018 NOI and 2020 extension order; Phase 1 abandonment completed June 29, 2019 per the operator's compliance filings referenced in the extension notice. Only the ~268-mile New Mexico/Arizona/Utah remainder (sold/transferred to the Navajo Tribal Utility Authority, serving Red Mesa, Kayenta, and Tuba City) is operating today. Per the batch instruction to 'distinguish the eastern segment operates from the pipeline operates': the EASTERN (NM/AZ/UT) segment operates; the pipeline as GEM currently attributes it (reaching California) does not. Status=operating is defensible ONLY if read as 'the surviving NM/AZ/UT segment is operating' -- the California endpoint and any capacity/length figure implying a live California connection is stale.

Roster check: no other PID in the 46-row US-West roster corresponds to Southern Trails or any segment/alias of it -- not a duplicate. Existence confirmed beyond doubt (multiple FERC dockets, an active operator website capture, and continuing trade coverage through at least 2020). Classification (gas pipeline) confirmed. This is one of three rows the batch brief flagged as having a plausible status issue; recommend adding a ResearcherNotes flag on Status (not changing Status itself, since the surviving segment genuinely operates) plus correcting EndState/Province and EndLocation off California to Arizona/Utah (the pipeline's current terminus serving Kayenta/Tuba City, AZ) -- see the paired Location finding below.

resolutions.researcher_notes:

This matches no documented configuration of the system: not the full historic converted system (~675-700 mi per the FERC FEIS notice: 592 mi of 16-in + 80 mi of 12-in + 3 mi of 22-in existing pipe, plus ~43.2 mi of new extensions), not the East Zone alone (~490 mi, Farmington NM to Essex CA per Wikipedia/background sources), and not the current surviving NM/AZ/UT remainder (~268 mi per NGI, after the ~220-mi CA/AZ abandonment). No single verified source states 405 mi / 651.8 km for any real segment of this pipeline.

UNRESOLVED as a positive value -- flagging as contested rather than proposing a replacement figure, because the surviving-segment mileage (~268 mi/431 km, NGI) is itself only single-sourced at medium confidence and I could not independently corroborate it against a second primary document (e.g., a current PHMSA annual report filing for the operating company) in the time available. CONTESTED (Owner1 / Owner1%): GEM records Owner1 = 'Southern Trails Pipeline Co' at 100%. This is the pre-2016 corporate name and is stale as a complete answer, but the successor picture is genuinely split rather than a single clean substitution: (1) Questar Corporation (parent of Southern Trails Pipeline Co) was acquired by Dominion Energy in 2016; Dominion's Questar Pipeline business (including Southern Trails) was then sold to Southwest Gas Holdings, closing Dec 31, 2021, and the surviving interstate-pipeline entities were rebranded 'MountainWest' effective April 1, 2022 -- a verified press release explicitly names a renamed subsidiary 'MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company.' (2) Separately and earlier, Dominion Energy negotiated to transfer/sell the operating (NM/AZ/UT) segment to the Navajo Tribal Utility Authority (NTUA) starting with a signing ceremony Nov 28, 2017, subject to FERC approval expected in 2018 -- consistent with the 2018 FERC NOI and the 2019-2020 abandonment/extension dockets for the California/Arizona legs. Two independent, both-naming sources establish the Owner1 field is at minimum stale, but they point to two different successor entities for two different aspects (corporate-name lineage vs. the operating segment's transfer to a tribal utility). Recommend NOT overwriting Owner1 with a single new value; instead flag as contested/needs-review with both candidate chains documented, and note in ResearcherNotes that a Update-leg pass should pull FERC eLibrary or a current PHMSA operator-of-record filing to resolve which entity (MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company vs. NTUA) is the current FERC-jurisdictional owner of record for the surviving segment.

resolutions.recommendation: change Status from 'operating' to 'retired' (as a gas pipeline) -- Trailblazer has been formally abandoned by FERC and physically repurposed to transport CO2, not natural gas; this is exactly the batch brief's flagged lead for P0266
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguous -- the pipeline is real, active infrastructure today (just not carrying gas). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster (P0151...P3601) -- no separate 'Trailblazer CO2' or similarly-named row exists, so this is not a redundancy question, only a status/classification one on this same row. CLASSIFICATION/STATUS (the batch brief's central lead): Tallgrass announced in 2022 that it would convert Trailblazer from natural gas to CO2 transport service. S&P Global (2022-06-01, via Wayback) reported Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC and Rockies Express Pipeline LLC filed for FERC authorization (Docket CP22-468, filed 2022-05-27) to abandon ~392 miles of the Trailblazer gas system in place and repurpose it for CO2, while gas shippers were to be rerouted onto new REX leased capacity/laterals. FERC's own Federal Register notice (2023-04-06) confirms an Environmental Assessment was issued for 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC, Rockies Express Pipeline LLC' covering this conversion. A second Federal Register notice (2024-10-09) confirms FERC's October 23, 2023 Order 'Issuing Certificate and Granting Abandonment' authorized the project (the 'Trailblazer Conversion Project' in Weld County, CO and Kimball County, NE), that construction began January 4, 2024, and that Trailblazer/REX requested (and were later granted, per the docket) an extension to complete the Hereford Ranch and Redtail Compressor Stations by December 23, 2024. Oil & Gas Journal (2024-05-06, via Wayback since the live OGJ URL serves randomized unrelated article content to non-browser fetches) reported Trailblazer/REX holding a CO2 transport open season under the FERC-approved conversion, confirming the project moved from authorization into commercialization. ADM's own investor-facing overview PDF states the timeline plainly: '2022 Announce Project ... 2024 Begin CO2 Service' and that the project 'converts the nearly 400-mile Trailblazer pipeline from natural gas service to carbon dioxide (CO2)... to permanently store more than 10 million metric tons of CO2 annually.' Nebraska Examiner (2025-09-24 and 2025-10-10) both independently confirm commercial CO2 shipments began October 3, 2025, moving CO2 from 11 Nebraska/Colorado/Wyoming ethanol plants ~392 miles to Wyoming for sequestration, explicitly stating 'the Trailblazer pipeline formerly carried natural gas' and 'much of the pipeline was already built as the natural gas line.' Pipeline & Gas Journal (2025-09, verified separately) restates the same 392-mile CO2-transport-begins story. Six independent origins (FERC/Federal Register x2, S&P Global, OGJ, ADM, Nebraska Examiner/PGJ) converge: Trailblazer is no longer in gas service. Per docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md, 'retired' is the correct Status value for a formally abandoned/decommissioned gas asset -- there is no 'converted' or repurposed-commodity value in the Status vocab, and this GGIT (gas) tracker is not the place to add a new CO2 row for the same pipe; that is a separate tracking-scope question for Baird, not resolved here. GEM's LastUpdated=2023-08-30 predates the October 2023 abandonment order and the 2024-2025 physical conversion/start of CO2 service, which is why the sheet is now stale rather than simply wrong-when-entered. NOTE for the batch brief's cross-reference: P0208 (TIGT/Pony Express Abandonment, Docket CP12-495, 2012-2014) is a DIFFERENT, EARLIER Tallgrass gas-to-crude conversion of a different pipeline (TIGT, not Trailblazer) -- confirmed by direct comparison of the two FERC dockets and Tallgrass's own 2016 10-K; the two conversions should not be conflated, and this row's finding stands independently of that one.

resolutions.recommendation: change StartState/Province from 'Wyoming' to 'Colorado' -- three independent sources place Trailblazer's origin in Colorado, not Wyoming
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM currently carries StartLocation='Cheyenne', StartState/Province='Wyoming'. Three independent origins instead describe a Colorado origin: (1) OSTI/DOE trade-journal abstract (1982): 'the Trailblazer Pipeline Co. 436-mile section from Rockport, Colo. to Beatrice [Neb.]'; (2) Tallgrass's own historical company-overview page (via a 2019-07-27 Wayback snapshot, since the live pipeline.tallgrassenergylp.com is now behind an Incapsula bot-wall for both live and later-dated Wayback crawls): 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC (Trailblazer) is a 436-mile pipeline extending from northeast Colorado to Gage County in Nebraska'; (3) Wikipedia's (en.wikipedia.org, independent of GEM/gem.wiki) 'Trailblazer Pipeline' stub, categorized under 'Natural gas pipelines in Colorado' and 'Natural gas pipelines in Nebraska' (NOT Wyoming), stating plainly it 'brings natural gas from Colorado into Nebraska.' The one source in tension with this is Tallgrass's own 2015 SEC S-1 registration statement, which hedges: 'The Trailblazer Pipeline is a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 436-miles of transportation pipelines that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska' -- consistent with an origin very close to the state line (Cheyenne, WY sits only a few miles north of the CO border; Rockport, CO sits just south of it) but not itself naming Wyoming as the state of origin. Weighing three independent, more specific sources (a contemporaneous trade journal, Tallgrass's own historical company page, and Wikipedia) against one hedged company-filing sentence, Colorado is the better-supported StartState/Province. Not proposing a specific StartLocation replacement (e.g. 'Rockport') given the S-1's own border-region framing and no fully independent second source for that particular place name -- leaving StartLocation as a lower-confidence open question rather than overreaching. EndLocation='Beatrice'/EndState/Province='Nebraska' are NOT contested -- all three of the above sources, plus the S-1, agree on the Nebraska/Beatrice-area terminus (the 2019 Tallgrass page's 'Gage County' is the same place -- Beatrice is the Gage County seat).

resolutions.recommendation: change StartYear1 from 1981 to 1982 -- the OSTI trade-journal source gives an explicit October 1982 completion date for the whole Trailblazer system, consistent with a 1981-1982 construction span rather than a 1981 in-service date
resolutions.researcher_notes: A federal-court opinion (Colo. Interstate Gas v. Natural Gas Pipeline Co., 661 F. Supp. 1448, D. Wyo. 1987, via Justia) states: 'In 1981-1982 a new pipeline, the Trailblazer System, was constructed to transport natural gas out of the Overthrust region of Wyoming.' The OSTI/DOE trade-journal abstract is more specific and gives a completion date: '...for an October 1982 completion date, the 36-in. Trailblazer pipeline system consists of three major segments...' Read together, construction began in 1981 (supporting a new ConstructionYear fill of 1981, below) and the system entered service/was completed in October 1982 -- not 1981 as GEM's StartYear1 currently states. Both sources describe the whole three-segment Trailblazer System (Overthrust + Wyoming Interstate/WIC + Trailblazer proper) as a single coordinated 1981-82 construction/completion event, so the October 1982 date applies to this Trailblazer segment as well. Tier kept at medium/high rather than higher because neither source gives a month-specific in-service date for the Trailblazer segment ALONE as distinct from the three-segment system, though OSTI's 'October 1982 completion date' is stated for the system as a whole in the same sentence that names the Trailblazer segment specifically.

resolutions.recommendation: clear FuelSource -- 'Colorado' is a state name, not an upstream field/plant/facility, and violates the documented GEM schema convention for this column
resolutions.researcher_notes: Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md's explicit documented gotcha, FuelSource (gas sheet) must name the upstream gas source feeding the line -- a specific field, plant, or facility (e.g. 'Abqaiq', 'Berri Gas Plant') -- and must NEVER be a state name or the commodity type. GEM's current value 'Colorado' is a state, not a named field/facility, so it is a schema-convention violation independent of the classification finding above. I could not confidently attribute a single named upstream field: Trailblazer historically received Rocky Mountain/Overthrust-belt gas (per the OSTI/Justia sources on the original three-segment Trailblazer System) via multiple interconnects rather than one dedicated field, and ADM's project-overview map depicts 'Cheyenne Hub' (a well-known multi-source trading/interconnect hub in the DJ Basin straddling the CO/WY line) near the pipeline's origin, but no source I found states outright that Cheyenne Hub (or any other single named point) IS Trailblazer's FuelSource in the GEM sense. Recommending the cell be cleared (left blank) rather than replaced with an unverified guess, per the schema doc's own instruction ('if you can't attribute one, leave it blank and note why -- do not default it'). This is also now moot with respect to the CO2 conversion: whichever way the classification question above is resolved, FuelSource as currently entered is a defect either way.

resolutions.recommendation: flag Capacity=878 MMcf/d as unconfirmed -- Tallgrass's own 2015 SEC S-1 states a different figure (902 MMcf/d) for the same pipeline
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's current Capacity (878.00 MMcf/d) could not be confirmed by any source I found. Tallgrass Energy Partners LP's SEC S-1 (filed 2015-02-24, CIK 0001633651) instead states: 'The Trailblazer Pipeline is a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 436-miles of transportation pipelines that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska with a total system design capacity of approximately 902 MMcf/d' (as of Dec 31, 2014). This is the pipeline's own regulated-entity's SEC disclosure, not a secondary aggregator, but it is a single origin, and I could not find a second independent source stating either 878 or 902 with confidence (a widely-mirrored 'design capacity as of 2016' figure of 878 MMcf/d traces to grokipedia.com, an AI-generated wiki that is not a citable/verifiable primary or secondary source, so I am not treating it as corroboration for GEM's existing value). Not proposing a firm replacement given the single-source status -- flagging the conflict so whoever next touches Capacity knows 878 is unconfirmed and 902 (2014-vintage, per the S-1) is the best-sourced alternative found so far.

resolutions.recommendation: No existence, duplicate, or classification concern. TransColorado Gas Transmission Company LLC is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipeline running from the Piceance/San Juan supply basins in northwest Colorado (Rio Blanco County) south to the San Juan Basin in northwest New Mexico (San Juan County), where it interconnects with El Paso Natural Gas and other systems. Confirmed independently via: (1) Kinder Morgan's own current (2026) corporate website listing it as an active wholly-owned natural gas pipeline asset; (2) two 1996/1998 Federal Register notices (FERC dockets CP95-79 and related) describing the same 22/24-inch, ~311-mile pipeline between the same two counties; (3) Kinder Morgan Inc.'s FY2012 SEC Form 10-K, which lists TransColorado among its wholly-owned gas pipeline assets with a 1.0 Bcf/d capacity figure; (4) El Paso Natural Gas Company's own 1996 SEC Form 10-Q, filed when El Paso still held a one-third ownership interest, independently corroborating the ~311-mile length and construction timeline; (5) offshore-technology.com/GlobalData profile; (6) Wikipedia. It is correctly classified as a distinct pipeline, NOT a duplicate of the two other 'Kinder Morgan Rockies trio' FERC systems flagged in the batch brief -- Colorado Interstate Gas (P0168) and Wyoming Interstate Company (P0282) are separate FERC-regulated entities/pipelines with their own certificated routes; none of the sources found for P0270 mention CIG or WIC facilities, and vice versa in cross-checks. CAVEAT (not escalated to a concern): offshore-technology.com's auto-generated 'location' schema snippet erroneously labels BOTH termini as 'Colorado' -- this is judged to be a GlobalData template/boilerplate artifact, contradicted by the weight of more precise, independent evidence (Kinder Morgan's own site, the 1996/1998 Federal Register notices, and Wikipedia) that consistently places the southern/eastern terminus in San Juan County, New Mexico. Ownership has consolidated over time from an original 1994-1995 three-way partnership (KN Energy Inc., Questar Pipeline Co., and El Paso Natural Gas Co., after El Paso bought Public Service Company of Colorado's original one-third stake in 1995) into a wholly-owned Kinder Morgan asset (KN Energy became Kinder Morgan Inc. via merger) -- this ownership evolution is historical background, not a current attribution error; GEM's Owner1='Kinder Morgan' 100% is CURRENT and correct.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Per batch guidance on the 'Kinder Morgan Rockies trio,' explicitly checked that no candidate reference for P0270 actually documents CIG or WIC facilities instead -- none did; the FERC dockets and county-level endpoints found are specific to TransColorado's own certificated route (Rio Blanco County, CO to San Juan County, NM).

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE is solid -- the underlying construction project is real and independently documented (FERC docket CP18-37-000, a new ~15,900 hp compressor station in Pima County, AZ; approved by FERC ~Oct 1-3, 2018 per Utility Dive, 'FERC authorizes expansion of US-Mexico pipeline', https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-authorizes-expansion-of-us-mexico-pipeline/538677/, published 2018-10-03, verified). What I actually verified: (1) Utility Dive (real content fetched and read directly, not just the search snippet -- the default url_verifier UA gets a 403 bot-wall on this host, but a browser UA gets 200 with the full article; same false-negative class the script's docstring already documents for other bot-walled hosts) states the CP18-37 compressor project raises Sierrita from 200,846 Dth/d to 'almost 323,000 Dth/d' (~323 MMcf/d total, i.e. a ~122,000 Dth/d increment), cost ~$56 million -- the SAME $56M figure gem.wiki attributes to 'Sierrita Pima Expansion' (P2615). (2) Kinder Morgan's own SEC Form 8-K earnings exhibit for Q4 2019 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506307/000150630720000002/kmi2019q48-kex991.htm, verified) describes a Sierrita expansion 'increas[ing] the pipeline's capacity by approximately 323,000 Dth/d to 524,000 Dth/d,' completion expected Q2 2020. (3) EIA's Today in Energy piece ({EIA}, verified) independently confirms a '0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion... completed in early 2020' -- 0.32 Bcf/d = 320 MMcf/d, matching P2615's recorded Capacity almost exactly, and NOT naming any separate 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' (4) Kinder Morgan's own FY2022 10-K ({KMI2022}, verified, page/line: 'Sierrita 35% 60 [miles] 0.52 [Bcf/d capacity]') reports Sierrita's TOTAL system capacity as of FY2022 as 0.52 Bcf/d = 520 MMcf/d -- i.e. 200 (original, confirmed via the 2018 10-K's '60 [miles] 0.20 [Bcf/d]' entry for the same asset) + 320 (Pima Expansion), with NO further increment for a separate 427 MMcf/d 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' If a second, independent 427 MMcf/d project had actually gone into service, KMI's own reported system capacity would be far higher than 520. (5) A Mexican federal government document (SENER/CRE status report, Oct 2017, https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/265260/Estatus_Gasoductos_octubre_2017.pdf, verified) lists the ORIGINAL Sierrita line (Tucson-Sasabe, 97 km, in service Dec 2014, Sierrita Gas LLC = MGI-Mitsui-KM) at 195 mmpcd capacity with a footnote that it 'sera expandida hasta 770 mmpcd' (will be expanded up to 770 mmpcd) per CFE's requirements -- a THIRD, still different, larger PLANNED ceiling figure from Oct 2017, distinct from both 627 and the 520/524 actually realized. This confirms 'Puerto Libertad' is the name of the Sonora town where a SEPARATE, IENova/CFE-owned Mexican pipeline (Sasabe-Pto. Libertad, 'Proyecto Noroeste' Tramo I, 218 km, also in service Dec 2014) receives Sierrita's exported gas -- i.e. 'Puerto Libertad' names the downstream Mexican market/destination the US compressor expansion was built to serve, not a second, separate US-side pipeline construction project. I could NOT independently verify the '627 MMcf/d' / '427 MMcf/d increment' figures against any primary document -- the only place they surfaced was gem.wiki's own narrative and one search-tool synthesized answer that also claimed the FederalRegister.gov notice states these numbers; when I fetched that exact URL directly, it returned FederalRegister.gov's bot-wall CAPTCHA page (title-tag text only, no article body), so that synthesis could not have come from the real page and should not be trusted -- flagging this as a near-miss so nobody downstream treats it as read. Net: P2614 and P2615 both describe -- with high confidence -- the SAME physical CP18-37 compressor project (same new compressor station in Pima County AZ, same $56M cost figure, same Oct 2018 FERC approval window, same 2020 completion), but carry two different, non-additive capacity figures (427 vs 320) neither of which, if simply added to each other or to the original 200, matches KMI's own verified FY2022 total of 520 MMcf/d. EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed via (1) EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (Historical Projects tab, downloaded and read locally per the source ladder — a fully independent US-government statistical source), which carries this exact project as 'Tuscarora Xpress Project', Operator 'TC Energy', Project Type 'Expansion', Pipeline Type 'Interstate', Authority 'FERC', Docket 'CP20-486', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2021-11-08, Year In Service 2021, Beg_State OR / End_State NV, Cost (millions) 13.45, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 15; and (2) three Federal Register notices in the same FERC docket (Notice of Application 2020-07-14/2020-15043; Notice of Intent to prepare an EA 2020-08-11/2020-17512; Notice of Schedule 2020-10-07/2020-22159), independently confirming the same scope, capacity (15,000 Dth/d), and Malin OR -> Wadsworth CS, Washoe County, NV routing. (3) TC Energy's own 'Tuscarora XPress Fact Sheet' (PDF, June 2020) gives the project schedule (Dec 2019 outreach, June 2020 file FERC application, June 2021 begin construction, Nov 2021 in-service) and confirms the scope is compressor replacement only, 'largely within the existing footprint.' EIA (independent) + FERC Federal Register (independent) + TC Energy fact sheet (operator) triangulate on every field on this row — see fills[] for the per-cell refs. VALUE CHECK: every recorded value (Capacity 15.00 MMcf/d, Length 0.00 km, Proposal 2020, Construction 2021, Start 2021, SegmentCost 13,450,000 USD) matches these sources exactly or within rounding (Capacity: 15,000 Dth/d ~ 15 MMcf/d given ~1,000-1,030 Btu/scf gas — EIA states 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 15' directly, an exact match; SegmentCost: EIA's 'Cost (millions) = 13.45' is an EXACT match to the sheet's 13,450,000 USD). DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate of P0275 (Tuscarora main system, 305 mi/miscoded as 305 km — see cross_row_leads) or of any other roster row; P3601 is the correctly-modeled incremental capacity-expansion phase of the same physical system, the same pattern the sweep brief already confirms for P2517/P2569/P2614/P2615. SOURCES OPENED: 8 of the 9 harvested wiki citations were opened/tested (bit.ly wiki citation resolved to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscarora_Gas_Pipeline — no XPress-specific content there; tcenergy.com/.../tuscarora-transmission-system/ — live, system-level page; tcplus.com/Tuscarora — live, operator asset-facts page; offshore-technology.com/.../tuscarora-gas-pipeline-the-us/ — live, system-level description; ceqanet.opr.ca.gov/1993112055/2 — live, 1994 CEQA record for the ORIGINAL 1990s pipeline, not the XPress increment; tcenergy.com/.../tuscarora-xpress-project/ — now 404, dead; tcenergy.com fact sheet PDF — live, read in full; ferc.gov/media/c-3-cp20-486-000-052021 — 403 to a scripted client, but the same docket (CP20-486) is fully corroborated via the three Federal Register notices and the EIA workbook, so the finding does not depend on this one dead link). The 9th harvested citation, eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, is a generic data hub (a mutable navigation surface, not independently citable per the source-ladder rule); I went straight to the specific dataset it points to — EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook — and read it locally, which is what actually supports the values below.

resolutions.recommendation: none — confirms the current Owner1 value; do not apply the batch brief's 'TC PipeLines LP is dissolved' premise to this pipeline
resolutions.researcher_notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE BATCH-WIDE GUIDANCE for this pipeline specifically: the scope brief states 'TC PipeLines LP is a dissolved entity' following the March 2021 TC Energy/TC PipeLines LP merger, and flags Owner1='TC PipeLines LP [100%]' on P3601 (and P0275) as stale on that basis. That premise does not hold for Tuscarora. The 2021 merger took TC PipeLines, LP PRIVATE (TC Energy acquired all publicly-held common units and it stopped trading on Nasdaq as 'TCP'), but the LP itself was NOT dissolved — it continues to exist as a distinct, wholly-owned reporting entity. TC Energy's own 'TC PipeLines, LP Consolidated Financial Statements' for Q4 2024 (published 2025) and referenced again in the 2025 statements both list 'Tuscarora Gas Transmission Company (Tuscarora)' as one of TC PipeLines LP's owned systems at 100 percent, as recently as December 31, 2024. tcplus.com (Tuscarora's own regulatory-postings site) independently states 'TC PipeLines, LP owns 100 percent of Tuscarora.' So Owner1='TC PipeLines LP' at 100% is CURRENT and correct as recorded — no change needed. Caveat: both of my confirming sources are TC Energy/TC PipeLines corporate-family disclosures (the operator's own audited financials + its own subsidiary's customer portal), not a third-party-independent source; I searched for an independent (non-TC-Energy) confirmation of the post-2021 ownership structure (S&P/Moody's rating commentary, trade press) and did not find one within the time available, so I'm flagging this as tier=medium on independence grounds even though the two sources are about as authoritative as this kind of fact gets (a subsidiary's own audited financial statements). This finding does not necessarily generalize to other rows in the batch that also carry 'TC PipeLines LP' — each should be checked against TC PipeLines LP's own current financial statements before being changed.

resolutions.recommendation: Location [ref] field values are scrambled across columns — move 'Wadsworth' from EndPrefecture/District into EndLocation; set EndPrefecture/District to 'Washoe County'; set StartPrefecture/District to 'Klamath County'
resolutions.researcher_notes: The Location [ref] unit's underlying content is correct (Malin, Oregon -> Wadsworth, Nevada) but two sub-fields are mis-mapped. The sheet currently has EndPrefecture/District='Wadsworth' and EndLocation=blank — but Wadsworth is a PLACE (the compressor station / community), which belongs in EndLocation, not a prefecture/district. The actual sub-state administrative unit — Washoe County, Nevada — is missing entirely. FERC's Notice of Application (Federal Register 2020-07-14/2020-15043) is explicit: the project runs 'from Malin, Oregon to the Wadsworth Compressor Station (CS) in Washoe County, Nevada.' Likewise StartPrefecture/District is blank; Malin, Oregon sits in Klamath County (Wikipedia, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malin,_Oregon, and consistent with every gazetteer entry for the city). EIA's workbook independently corroborates the state-level termini (Beg_State=OR, End_State=NV). Net effect: the values on the sheet are directionally right, but the district/prefecture columns need the county names, and 'Wadsworth' needs to move from EndPrefecture/District to EndLocation.
